description: Per-character cursed-energy level thresholds (gauge levels and the spendable-pool cap) and recovery timing/rates for that pool.

Id.simple: Character/row ID used to find this cursed-energy row.
Id.technical: Exported as FName ID; the native UPROPERTY is Id and the table's ImportKeyField is Id. AGameCharacter::ResolveDataRows searches DTM.CharacterCursedEnergyDataTables with FStudioBattleCharacterOverrides.CursedEnergyIdOverride when it is non-None, otherwise CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterCursedEnergy; a miss fails character setup. MissionCharacterDataTable supplies those overrides (for example STMSN_09104M_ALLY_01 uses CP_020_ST instead of CP_020). Battle HUD widgets GameCommandListWidget and GameVsEnemyIntervalCharacterWidget instead look rows up directly by Character->Id_CharacterCursedEnergy and do not apply the mission override. All 36 exported row names match their ID values.

LevelThreshold.simple: Increasing gauge amounts that define cursed-energy levels 1-4 and the spendable-energy cap for the reached level.
LevelThreshold.technical: TArray<float>. All 36 exported rows have exactly four positive, strictly increasing values (CP_010: 100/200/300/400; CP_020_ST reuses CP_020's thresholds). GetCursedEnergyLevel counts entries <= CursedEnergyGauge and floors the result at 1. InitializeStatus uses [0] as the gauge floor and copies the array into LevelThresholdDeltas (walked backwards, a[i] -= a[i-1]) for HUD markers. SetCursedEnergyGauge clamps the gauge to [LevelThreshold[0], LevelThreshold[CursedEnergyLevelMax]]; CursedEnergyLevelMax is Setup.Int40 (default 3, battle rules can set 0..3) and is an index, not necessarily the array's last element. On a level change it sets CursedEnergyMax = LevelThreshold[NewLevel - 1], adds the threshold delta to energy, and applies level effects. The out-of-line helper treats Level as 1-based and returns 0 for a null row or out-of-range index; CP_220 and CN_240 carry the same helper body. Other readers assume the four-entry shape: GetLastLevelThreshold uses fixed [3] (also used for CP_110/CP_130/CP_250 energy and exp), passive exp uses .Last(), resets use [0], and link-combo/CP_220 interpolate adjacent levels. A shorter exported array would be unsafe in those paths.

Recover_Wait.simple: Delay before the cursed-energy pool starts regenerating after a drop or level-up.
Recover_Wait.technical: Seconds of scaled wait time. SetCursedEnergy sets CursedEnergyRecoverWait = GetStatusRate154() * (SoloSide == 1 ? Recover_Wait_Rate_Solo : 1.0f) * Recover_Wait when the incoming value is below current energy; level-up uses only the solo multiplier times Recover_Wait. Tick subtracts GetActionValue112() * DeltaTime, floored at zero, and adds no recovery while the wait is still > 0. GetActionValue112 is an action-layer product that can be 0 (for example CP_121 with shikigami 1 out, or attacks with bRecoverCursedEnergyDisabled), so the real-time delay can be longer or indefinite. Constructor default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 1.5, and the 36 rows span 0.5-2.0.

Recover_Speed.simple: Cursed energy restored per second after the recovery wait expires.
Recover_Speed.technical: Base energy units/second. Tick passes CursedEnergy + GetCursedEnergyRecoverRate() * (SoloSide == 1 ? Recover_Speed_Rate_Solo : 1.0f) * Recover_Speed * DeltaTime to SetCursedEnergy, which clamps to [0, CursedEnergyMax]. GetCursedEnergyRecoverRate itself aggregates chase/escape and buff rates with action-controller/action-layer multipliers, so this field is only the row-level base rate. Constructor default 0.0f; CP_010 exports 75.0, and the 36 rows span 50-200.

Recover_Wait_Rate_Solo.simple: Solo-only multiplier on the recovery wait.
Recover_Wait_Rate_Solo.technical: Float read only when FGameCharacterStatusSetup.SoloSide == 1. Level-up sets the wait to this * Recover_Wait; SetCursedEnergy sets it to GetStatusRate154() * this * Recover_Wait. Non-solo paths use 1.0. All 36 rows export 1.0 (no change); the row-struct constructor default is 0.0f, so an omitted serialized property would zero the wait.

Recover_Speed_Rate_Solo.simple: Solo-only multiplier on the cursed-energy recovery rate.
Recover_Speed_Rate_Solo.technical: Float used in place of 1.0 in the tick recovery product when Setup.SoloSide == 1; non-solo uses 1.0. The wait logic and SetCursedEnergy's clamp do not read it. All 36 rows export 1.0; the row-struct constructor default is 0.0f, so an omitted serialized property would disable regeneration for solo sides.

Add_Rate_Solo.simple: Serialized solo add-rate field with no identified consumer in this reconstruction.
Add_Rate_Solo.technical: Native float at retail row offset 0x30, corroborated by the layout check and retail reflection dump. All 36 rows export 1.0 (neutral if it is used as a multiplier), and the row-struct constructor default is 0.0f. AddCursedEnergyExp only forwards its Exp argument to SetCursedEnergyGauge and plays level-down FX; it never reads this row field. No direct or copied read of Add_Rate_Solo exists in Source/Plugins, so its exact formula and purpose cannot be established from available evidence and must not be inferred from the name.

notes: CursedEnergyGauge (the level/exp gauge) and CursedEnergy (the spendable pool) are separate status fields. LevelThreshold determines both the level count and CursedEnergyMax (Threshold[NewLevel - 1]); Recover_Wait and Recover_Speed with their solo multipliers affect only the spendable pool. Initialization sets the gauge to Threshold[0] and then sets CursedEnergy to CursedEnergyMax.

Data relationships verified in the exports: CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterCursedEnergy selects the default row, while MissionCharacterDataTable can override it (STMSN_09104M_ALLY_01 and STMSN_09106M_ALLY_01 -> CP_020_ST; STMSN_09112M_ENEMY_01 -> CN_122_ST). The _ST rows keep the base thresholds but use shorter waits and faster recovery (0.5 s / 150 or 200 versus 1.0 s / 90 or 110). The 34 per-character export folders are views into the same 36-row table, not additional rows.
No language-localized table asset was exported; the catalog and export contain one CharacterCursedEnergyDataTable variant with 36 rows, including the two _ST rows named above.

GetCursedEnergyLevelThreshold takes a 1-based Level and returns 0 for an invalid index, while GetCursedEnergyLevel returns at least 1; fixed reads of [0]/[3] and .Last() assume the shipped four-entry arrays. CursedEnergyLevelMax is a configurable threshold index (usually 3; battle rules can lower it) and the HUD's clamped level is min(CursedEnergyLevel, 3).
Add_Rate_Solo is serialized, retail-layout-verified, and constant 1.0 in the exported data, but no consumer is present in this source snapshot; its purpose remains unresolved.

Behavior is described from reconstructed C++ with retail RVA/offset annotations, plus retail reflection/layout dumps and row exports. No retail Blueprint graph or Blueprint logic evidence was available or used, so no Blueprint-derived claims are made.

usages.detail: Resolves the table by the exact name CharacterCursedEnergyDataTable into the manager's CharacterCursedEnergyDataTables array.
Override-aware lookup caches the row in AGameCharacter.CursedEnergyRow; a miss fails character setup.
Initialization starts the gauge at Threshold[0], then initializes CursedEnergy from CursedEnergyMax.
Copies LevelThreshold into LevelThresholdDeltas and converts it to per-level deltas for HUD markers.
Counts thresholds at or below the gauge to compute the cursed-energy level, floored at 1.
Tests Threshold[CursedEnergyLevelMax] against the gauge for the at-threshold condition.
Clamps the level gauge to Threshold[0] and Threshold[CursedEnergyLevelMax].
On level-up, applies the solo wait multiplier to Recover_Wait and uses the new threshold as CursedEnergyMax.
On an energy drop, sets the wait using GetStatusRate154, the solo wait rate, and Recover_Wait.
Indirect wait consumer: the action-layer product can make GetActionValue112 zero, pausing wait decay.
Uses the last threshold to scale cursed-energy exp gained passively with time.
Applies Recover_Speed and Recover_Speed_Rate_Solo each tick once the wait expires.
GetLastLevelThreshold reads fixed Threshold[3], also used by CP_110/CP_130/CP_250.
Round/knock-out resets return the gauge to Threshold[0] before refilling the pool to its max.
Link-combo gain interpolates between adjacent values from the same threshold array.
Tag-combo exit refills each performer to the clamped next level's threshold.
Shared 1-based LevelThreshold[Level - 1] accessor returns 0 for a null row or bad index.
Charge interpolation uses thresholds for base, next-stage and maximum gauge values.
Adaptation completion refills CN_240 to the clamped next level's threshold.
Passes status-derived threshold deltas and reachable level into the battle HUD gauge.
Places HUD threshold markers at running 0.01-scaled positions derived from the deltas.
Direct, override-free lookup converts LevelThreshold entries to integer deltas for command-list markers.
Direct, override-free lookup copies LevelThreshold into the versus-enemy interval gauge.
